% --- latex-dual-layer macros (auto-generated) ---
\newlength{\dlboxwidth}
\newlength{\dlboxheight}
\newlength{\dlboxdepth}
\newcommand{\duallayerbox}[2]{%
  \begingroup
  \settowidth{\dlboxwidth}{\strut #1}%
  \settoheight{\dlboxheight}{\strut #1}%
  \settodepth{\dlboxdepth}{\strut #1}%
  \ifdim\dlboxwidth=0pt
    \settowidth{\dlboxwidth}{#2}%

\section*{Multiple Choice (10 marks)}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item \duallayerbox{In adolescence:}{In early childhood:}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item Girls physiologically increase their percentage body fat
    \item Brain growth is faster than at any other stage in life
    \item Type 1 obesity related diabetes is most common
    \item Peak bone mass occurs before the growth spurt ends
    \item Type 2 obesity related diabetes remains a very rare problem
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Parasympathetic preganglionic nerves leave the central nervous system with the}{Optic nerve fibres leave the central nervous system with the}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item eighth cranial nerves.
    \item second cranial nerves.
    \item first cranial nerves.
    \item fifth cranial nerves.
    \item sixth cranial nerves.
\end{enumerate}
\item Which of the following could very well be a cohort difference rather than a change that
occurs with age?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item Loss of muscle mass
    \item Shrinkage of the thymus gland
    \item Differences in weight
    \item Changes in metabolism rate
    \item Changes in eyesight
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Blood clots are responsible for repeatedly blocking a catheter.}{The catheter itself appears damaged and is repeatedly failing.} What should you do?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item Use a syringe to remove the clot.
    \item Remove the catheter and recatheterize.
    \item Replace the catheter with a new one without informing medical staff.
    \item Inform the patient's family.
    \item Inform the patient.
\end{enumerate}
\item Which of the following is true about \duallayerbox{rectal bleeding}{anal fissure}?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item Hemorrhoids are never a cause of rectal bleeding
    \item A painful digital examination suggests an anal fissure
    \item A colonoscopy is not necessary if rectal bleeding is present
    \item Rectal cancer is the commonest cause of rectal bleeding
    \item Bright red blood on the finger usually signifies a caecal lesion
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\item True or False: \duallayerbox{Niacin and riboflavin}{Vitamin C and folate} are the vitamins that are lost most readily during cooking.
\item True or False: The worldwide prevalence of obesity is approximately 13\%, indicating a significant public health concern.
\end{enumerate}
